chapter: Theater work, first jobs and recording credits
title: Frank Paisley and Brother Red
summary: He identifies Frank Paisley, his boyhood friend and recording sideman.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well I just went and took a fellow, his name is Mio Ink Weave, they called him Ink. And I just approached him and told him I had a band. I had a line of some good fellows like Shirley Clay, George Reynolds, Artis Torks, myself, and George Reynolds. And this boy, another boy I was raised up, just lived in, Frank. Frank.
Yeah. We were raised up together. He lived just two, he lived on Louie's End Avenue and I lived on Willow between me and General Taylor. Yeah. He recorded with me. Later on he went to California.
And you kept playing music up until yesterday? No. Do you know Frank Paisley? Real bright fellow?
That's the same fellow. Yeah. It's different than his name. Some people. Red. He was up there. He called him Paisley. Brother Red.

He used to play this boy that plays mostly in Texas there. What's his, Dominick's nephew? Albert. Don Albert. Don Albert. Don Albert, yeah. I saw him in the picture. The end of the band there, Frank. Yeah, we were raised together. That's the same as Frank Paisley. The same.
Yeah, well you know Richard M. Jones calls him Brother Red on the record.

I think it's Dusty Bottom. Yeah, that's the same as Frank Paisley. Yeah, well Richard M. Jones calls him Brother Red on the record. Yeah. I think it's Dusty Bottom.
